title: Redwood POC weekly sync - benchmark review vs baseline
meeting_header: Date: 2025-03-26 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 40m | Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM); Alex, Priya, Carlos, Janelle (FinSight)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results for Redwood runtime vs baseline provider. Discussed latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput under concurrent load, effect of batching and KV cache, sequence length mix, and next steps to run dedicated-pool test and share raw CSVs + tuning recommendations. Several minor transcription glitches; technical questions from SRE about warm-up behavior and tail latency.
topics: Benchmark results: latency and throughput comparison
Workload characterization: sequence lengths and concurrency
Tuning: batching, prefix caching, quantization profiles
Next steps: dedicated pool run, share raw results, pricing/security docs
transcript: [00:00] Sofia Ramirez (AE): hey everyone thanks for hopping on, um this is our weekly poc sync with finsight. quick roll call?
[00:07] Alex Kim (FinSight): alex here, priya, carlos and janelle are on as well. hey sofia.
[00:12] Daniel Cho (SE): hi team, daniel from redwood se. i'll run through the bench high level then dive into the p95/p99 stuff.

[00:20] Priya Nair (FinSight): cool, we got your note earlier with the charts — thanks. main thing we want to see is tail latency under 250ms for p95 on our 512 token average prompts, and throughput to match baseline at peak concurrency.

[00:35] Daniel Cho (SE): right yes, so quick context: we ran the same model family you gave us — 34B-ish open model — on our hosted infra and compared to your baseline provider (BaselineVendor in your deck). workloads were two mixes: read-heavy (short 64 tokens) and mixed (avg 512, some 1024 spikes).
[00:53] Sofia Ramirez (AE): i'll flag that the baseline run was done with their recommended batching. we tried to mirror batch sizes but there may be slight differences in warmup procedure.
[01:05] Carlos Mendes (FinSight): can you walk the numbers? p50/p95/p99 and rps at concurrency 100 and 300?

[01:12] Daniel Cho (SE): sure. high level: p50 is comparable, redwood p95 is 180ms on mixed workload vs baseline 230ms, p99 is 420ms vs baseline 510ms. throughput at conc 100: redwood 420 rps vs baseline 390 rps. at conc 300: redwood 1.1k rps vs baseline 950 rps. those are median runs across three repeats.
[01:45] Janelle Ford (Product): those p99 numbers are promising. what's causing the p99 improvement?

[01:50] Daniel Cho (SE): two big things — our continuous batching with latency-aware batching knobs and prefix/K-V cache hit rates. also kernel selection for attention optimized the long tails. small caveat: quantization profile we used was 4-bit for the vram-limited nodes, baseline used int8 on different hw which explains some differences.
[02:10] Alex Kim (FinSight): when you say K-V cache, is that persistent across requests in a session? we rely on multi-turn chat workloads, so warm-start matters.

[02:18] Daniel Cho (SE): yes, prefix kv caching persists per conversation session when pinned; we saw a 30-45% token compute reduction on repeated contexts leading to lower tail latency after warm-up. caveat: if you route to different nodes without sticky session you lose the cache — that's in our run config we pinned to single pool.
[02:40] Priya Nair (FinSight): warm-up behavior — baseline seemed to get a bit faster after 10 minutes. did you run steady-state long enough?

[02:47] Daniel Cho (SE): good call, our runs had a 12-minute ramp and then three 10-minute steady windows. i can share raw CSVs. sometimes the transcriber flips numbers — uh, the csv has the correct timestamps.
[03:05] Carlos Mendes (FinSight): any differences in response truncation or tokenization that could affect latency?

[03:10] Daniel Cho (SE): we used the same tokenizer you provided when possible; we also normalized max output tokens to 512 to keep parity. slight differences in stop token handling can add a few ms on average but not p99.
[03:28] Sofia Ramirez (AE): quick interjection — security question from janelle earlier: did we run with encryption at rest and KMS?
[03:34] Daniel Cho (SE): yes, for the private run we enabled customer-managed KMS; for hosted POC the logs are encrypted and access is RBAC-limited. we'll send SOC2 artifact today per your request.
[03:45] Janelle Ford (Product): perfect, plz include a note on audit log retention — legal asked about 1 year retention options.
[03:52] Maya Patel (CSM): noted, sending SOC2 + security whitepaper and retention options after call.
[04:00] Alex Kim (FinSight): digging into tuning — what are the quick wins we can try this week? batching or quantization?

[04:06] Daniel Cho (SE): batching config is the easiest: reduce max batch size for latency-critical routes, or enable latency-targeted batching which drops batch wait time at slight throughput cost. quantization: try a mixed profile for the heaviest models — 4-bit for feed-forward and 8-bit for attention gave good latency/quality tradeoff in our tests.
[04:30] Priya Nair (FinSight): any quality regressions observed with 4-bit? we need to keep rouge/bleu within 1-2% of baseline for our evaluation prompts.
[04:37] Daniel Cho (SE): we ran your eval set — quality delta was within 0.8% on average; a couple prompts had small differences we can annotate. we'll attach the eval diff csv.
[04:49] Carlos Mendes (FinSight): tail-latency mitigation — what about routing fallback? if we hit dedicated capacity limits, will requests go to hosted lower-tier models?

[04:56] Sofia Ramirez (AE): yes, redwood supports smart routing policies. in your poc we set fallback to a cost-tier model with same family; we can change policy per route if you want strict SLOs to avoid fallback.
[05:10] Alex Kim (FinSight): ok that's important. can we simulate a noisy neighbor event and see behavior?
[05:14] Daniel Cho (SE): yes we'll run a noisy neighbor test on the dedicated pool next run; that'll show tail effects and routing triggers.
[05:22] Priya Nair (FinSight): timeline — if you run dedicated pool tests this week can we get results before our steering committee next Tuesday?
[05:28] Sofia Ramirez (AE): yes, daniel and team can run dedicated pool test Thu-Fri and we can share results by Monday EOD. we'll also include raw CSVs and the benchmarking script.
[05:40] Janelle Ford (Product): pricing ask — if performance delta holds, what's the delta vs baseline on cost per 1M tokens?

[05:46] Sofia Ramirez (AE): i'll have finance provide a model estimate. quick note: unit cost depends heavily on batch sizing and cache hit rates; we'll give a range and a pivot table with your observed hit rates.
[06:00] Alex Kim (FinSight): action items and owners?
[06:03] Sofia Ramirez (AE): sure, let's list them out
[06:05] (short pause as people update their notes)

[06:15] Sofia Ramirez (AE): recap: daniel to run dedicated-pool noisy-neighbor test and share raw CSVs by 2025-03-28; maya to send SOC2/security whitepaper and retention options today; sofia to share pricing model and pivot table by 2025-03-31; daniel to share eval diffs and tuning recommendation doc by 2025-03-28.
[06:45] Alex Kim (FinSight): sounds good. one more Q — routing across regions, we saw slightly higher cross-region latency in earlier test. is regional routing automatic?

[06:52] Daniel Cho (SE): smart routing can prefer region affinity; for the poc we pinned region to us-east to avoid cross-region variance. if you need multi-region low-latency we can propose geo-routing with warm caches per region.
[07:05] Priya Nair (FinSight): ok let's pause there, appreciate the run-through. we'll review the CSVs and schedule a follow up after the dedicated test.
[07:12] Sofia Ramirez (AE): thanks all, we'll send notes and raw files. meeting adjourned.
[07:18] (meeting ends)
